sources.name: The Guardian Technology
sources.title: Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO
sources.text: Chipmaker reverses decision it made to remove chief executive after reports of affairs including with alleged Chinese spy Nvidia has said it is reinstating Jensen Huang as chief executive, effective immediately, just weeks after his dramatic resignation after reports of extramarital affairs including with an alleged Chinese spy. Nvidia shares surged on the news, jumping more than 25% in premarket trading. The tech company’s move to bring Huang back marks a sharp reversal from its board’s decision just days earlier to rule out his return. Huang built Nvidia from a video-game chip designer into the dominant supplier of AI processors, steering its roadmap, customer deals and Washington ties along the way. He resigned on 12 November after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with a businesswoman US authorities suspect of spying for China, an allegation Beijing denies. The board said it was satisfied with Huang’s candour and leadership ability and, after receiving input from senior US government officials, saw no national security risk in his return. Donald Trump called for Huang’s reinstatement overnight, posting on Truth Social: “I hope the Board of Nvidia rehires Jensen Huang . It would be the best thing for the Company, and also, for the U.S.A. President DONALD J. TRUMP.”

sources.name: CNBC Technology
sources.title: Nvidia skyrockets 30% on Huang’s return as CEO, recovering nearly all the losses since he disclosed affair
sources.text: Nvidia on Monday announced Jensen Huang has been reinstated as CEO, effective immediately, a dramatic twist in a scandal that hammered the chipmaker's stock price and rocked tech and artificial intelligence industries. The board of directors said it unanimously voted to reinstate Huang following "a series of discussions and meetings" with him. The board added that it "received input from senior levels of the United States government" that it is confident that Huang's reinstatement "poses no national security risk." Shares of Nvidia surged 31% following the announcement. Huang resigned from his role as chief executive earlier this month after a series of shocking reports about multiple extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. The New York Times reported on Sunday that the woman, Alice Huang, was in contact with an officer at China's Ministry of State Security during at least part of the time that she was engaging in a relationship with Huang. "I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution," Huang said in a statement. "I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process." President Donald Trump celebrated Huang's return to Nvidia on Monday, writing in a post on his social media site that the board made "the correct and proper decision" to reinstate him. Trump said the U.S. needs Huang's leadership to "ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy." He reiterated that the U.S. government has "no reason to believe" that Huang's return poses a risk to national security, and that it "does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct." "On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure," Trump wrote. Nvidia did not immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment on Huang's reinstatement. For weeks following Nvidia's ouster, the company's board maintained that it was not considering Huang's reinstatement. It appointed Colette Kress, Nvidia's CFO, as the chipmaker's interim CEO, who reiterated that position in an interview with CNBC following Huang's ouster. Nvidia's board formed an independent committee and hired the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct an investigation into Huang and whether company secrets or national security were compromised. The board said Monday that "the committee's investigation will proceed to conclusion" and that Huang is "committed to cooperating with it." "The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Nvidia Board Chair Harvey Jones said in a statement. "We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company. This is breaking news. Please refresh for updates.

sources.text: Apenas once días después de su salida, Nvidia ha anunciado oficialmente que su fundador recupera los cargos de CEO y presidente de la compañía, además de su puesto en el consejo de administración. La decisión se ha tomado por unanimidad y tiene efecto inmediato, y la vuelta de Huang se produce tras una crisis que había puesto en jaque no solo la estabilidad de la empresa, sino de toda una industria. El Gobierno de EEUU, clave . En el comunicado se incluye un comentario especialmente llamativo: el consejo recibió información de altos cargos del Gobierno estadounidens, y con dicha información consideró que el regreso de Huang no suponía un riesgo para la seguridad nacional. La empresa también asegura que las conversaciones mantenidas con el directivo han despejado sus dudas sobre su sinceridad y capacidad para seguir dirigiéndola. Donald Trump llegó a insinuar estos días que Huang recuperaría su puesto, pero en Nvidia no indican si dichos comentarios influyeron o no en la decisión. Giro de 180 grados . Lo sorprendente es que hace apenas seis días la propia Nvidia descartaba totalmente la vuelta de su líder . Harvey Jones, presidente del consejo, había asegurado que la empresa no tenía intención de readmitirlo y que buscaría un nuevo CEO. Ahora ese mismo consejo ha cambiado totalmente de idea y decide que Huang es la persona adecuada para dirigir Nvidia. El origen del escándalo . La crisis comenzó cuando salieron a la luz las relaciones extramatrimoniales de Huang. Una de ellas fue con Alice Huang, vinculada a Megaspeed, una empresa de Singapur investigada por posibles desvíos de chips avanzados de Nvidia a China. Los servicios de inteligencia de EEUU sospechan además que Alice Huang podría tener vínclos con los servicios de inteligencia chinos, algo que negaron desde Pekín. Luego aparecerían informaciones sobre otra relación de Huang con una subordinada, lo que acabó precipitando los acontecimientos y la dimisión de Huang. Las sospechas de espionaje no han sido demostradas, y no hay evidencias claras de que Huang filtrara información confidencial. Pero la investigación continúa . Nvidia ha querido dejar claro que la reincorporación no supone el fin del proceso de investigación. El comité independiente creado para averiguar si Huang fue objeto de una operación de inteligencia extranjera seguirá trabajando hasta llegar a sus conclusiones, y el propio Huang se ha comprometido a colaborar. Además la compañía ha creado un comité especializado en seguridad nacional y controles de exportación y tendrá un responsable directo del cumplimiento normativo. Aunque Huang recupera su puesto, de cara al público habrá refuerzo de los mecanismos de vigilancia que rodean el negocio. Los inversores querían a Huang . La noticia ha provocado una reacción espectacular en bolsa, con subidas que han superado el 30% durante la negociación. Lo que ha ocurrido en Wall Street es una clara demostración de la relevancia que el mercado tecnológico concede al fundador de Nvidia, cuya dirección ha sido fundamental para convertir a la empresa en la gran joya de la industria de la IA. Como explicábamos en Xataka, su salida también había dejado clara una debilidad estructural: Nvidia depende enormemente de Huang y no había sucesor claro que pudiese coger las riendas. Eso es algo que ahora quizás Huang deba comenzar a preparar. Once días de vorágine . Colette Kress, directora financiera de Nvidia, había asumido temporalmente las funciones de CEO mientras el consejo buscaba sustituto/a para el cargo. La CEO interina también dejó claro que Huang no volvería a su puesto hace unos días, lo que parecía negar dicha opción por completo. Ahora Kress volverá a centrarse en la responsabilidad que ocupaba previamente. Mientras, Huang ha agradecido el apoyo de los empleados, accionistas y socios, y asegura regresar con humildad y un compromiso renovado. El fundador recupera así prácticamente todo el poder ejecutivo que había perdido tras su dimisión, aunque sin duda habrá una supervisión más estricta tras este regreso. Pero . La crisis de Nvidia ha puesto de manifiesto hasta qué punto las relaciones personales de un directivo pueden tener un impacto geopolítico colosal. Los chips de Nvidia son foco claro de la guerra comercial y tecnológica entre EEUU y China, y las decisiones sobre quién puede acceder a dichos chips tienen consecuencias sobre toda la industria tecnológica y de la IA. Que el Gobierno de EEUU haya influido de tal forma en ese regreso también deja claro hasta qué punto Nvidia ha dejado de ser una empresa tecnológica convencional y es más bien una importante pieza de ese gran puzzle geopolítico en el que se ha convertido todo el segmento.

sources.title: Jensen Huang Is Back as Nvidia CEO
sources.text: Jensen Huang is stepping back into his role as chief executive of Nvidia effective immediately. The stunning reversal comes 11 days after Huang resigned as CEO from the company he cofounded 33 years ago, and after multiple declarations from the board of directors that it had no intention of reinstating him. On Monday, they took a conciliatory tone. “The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners, and customers,” said recently appointed board chair Harvey Jones in a press release announcing the decision. In that announcement the board said it was “satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead Nvidia,” and that it had “received input from senior levels of the United States government” on the way to its decision. On Monday morning, President Donald Trump posted that the Nvidia board “has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO.” “I am honored to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” said Huang in a statement. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment.” Huang resigned as Nvidia’s CEO on November 12, and longtime chief financial officer Colette Kress was installed as his interim replacement. Five days later, Huang publicly announced that he was open to resuming his role as chief executive, noting the “outpouring of calls” from “employees, investors, business partners, and customers” advocating for his return. “If the board of directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO,” Huang wrote. The day Huang resigned, many Nvidia employees spoke up in his support. As reported by WIRED, employees left more than 1,600 comments on an internal “suggestion box” post in which they urged the company’s board to reinstall him as CEO. In the days following, a public petition calling for Huang’s reinstatement began circulating. At the time of writing, it has amassed more than 200,000 online signatures, the majority of whom self-identified as Nvidia shareholders. Tech elites like Elon Musk and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan have claimed that they were going to sign the petition or had signed it. Huang’s reinstatement marks a total reversal from the public stance of Nvidia’s board of directors, which said during the company’s November 17 earnings call that it “does not intend” to reinstate him as CEO. WIRED has further reported that the board was alarmed by what one source described as Huang’s “lying” over the last year or so. President Donald Trump, who developed a close working relationship with Huang during his second administration, had indicated openness to Huang returning as CEO. Trump told reporters on November 16 that he “would not mind” if Huang returned as chief executive, adding that he believed he had “learned a big lesson.” Huang’s resignation followed days of scrutiny over several extramarital romantic relationships: one with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who has no known relation to Jensen, one with a Nvidia employee who directly reported to Huang, and one with a different Nvidia employee. Huang’s relationship with Alice became the subject of particularly intense focus on November 6, when The New York Times and Financial Times reported that US intelligence officials suspected that Alice may be an asset of the Chinese Ministry of State Security, both citing an intelligence briefing that circulated among top Trump administration officials last year. In the days since, some reports and Trump administration officials have questioned the accuracy of that intelligence. The Chinese government has consistently rejected claims that Alice was one of its spies. Alice was the chief executive of Megaspeed, a Singapore-based AI company that’s been accused of helping Chinese tech companies use Nvidia’s most advanced chips at overseas locations, effectively sidestepping US export restrictions. Alice has also reportedly worked as a television reporter, at HSBC's Hong Kong-based private banking arm , and at an investment bank backed by the Chinese state. Huang cofounded Nvidia in 1993 with Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem, purportedly with the mission of bringing realistic 3D graphics to personal computers. For many years, the company was primarily known within the gaming community . It didn’t become a household name until the recent AI boom, when its graphic processing units (GPUs) became a crucial piece of infrastructure for powering advanced AI models. Nvidia controlled about 90 percent of the global GPU market as of September 2026. The year prior, it became the first ever company to be valued at more than $4 trillion, though its stock price has been in precipitous decline since Huang’s resignation. This is a developing story. Please check back for updates.

sources.name: CNBC Technology
sources.title: Tech stocks rally after Nvidia board approves Jensen Huang's return as CEO
sources.text: Major tech stocks rebounded across the board Monday, following Friday's steep sell-off when artificial intelligence stocks fell in the Nasdaq's worst week since 2020. Shares of Nvidia surged 30% after Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO of the company. Nvidia's surge and Huang's reinstatement follow a more than 40% slump in the stock over the past month, as Huang was ousted as CEO of the company he founded after he admitted to having an extramarital affair with a woman U.S. intelligence reportedly believes to be a Chinese spy. The Nasdaq slid 10% last week and opened over 6% higher Monday. All three major averages ended last week in correction territory, and the Nasdaq turned negative for 2026. Tech stocks remain rocky as investors remain nervous about the valuation of some AI companies and business models. Stocks of Big Tech companies and other stocks related to the AI trade also saw a lift Monday after the Nvidia news. Alphabet stock surged 6%, while Meta added over 5%, Amazon was up nearly 5% and Microsoft jumped 4%. SpaceX was up 9% and AMD added over 8.5%. Neoclouds, which have seen a particularly choppy few months, surged. Nebius was up over 30%, CoreWeave 28% and Iren 28%. Anthropic shares were trading flat after a brief premarket surge, in its third day of trading following its initial public offering on Thursday. Anthropic raised a record $93.5 billion in its IPO. The stock gained 17% in its debut on Thursday, before closing 8.5% down on Friday.

sources.text: So much for the board not intending to bring him back. NVIDIA has reversed course and reinstated Jensen Huang as its CEO and president, effective immediately. The board said in a statement it held a series of meetings and discussions with Huang, who resigned 11 days ago following reports of multiple affairs. It added that it had "received input from senior levels of the United States government" and determined that reinstating Huang posed no risk to national security. "I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution," Huang said. "I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading NVIDIA during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can't wait to get back to work." NVIDIA said the board members voted unanimously to reappoint Huang, just a few days after chair Harvey Jones said on an earnings call that they did "not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO." In his first public statement since stepping down on November 12, Huang said last week he "would be honored" to return to the helm of the company he cofounded, noting that he'd "seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA's employees, investors, business partners and customers" for him step back into the CEO position.

sources.text: In a stunning reversal, Nvidia’s board said on Monday that it had reinstated Jensen Huang as the company’s CEO and president, less than two weeks after he resigned following his admission of at least two extramarital affairs, including one with a woman whom the U.S. government suspects to be a Chinese spy. The decision marks an extraordinary comeback for one of the tech industry’s most influential executives, whose abrupt departure raised questions about national security and the future of the world’s most valuable chipmaker. Notably, the U.S. government itself played a role in his return: Nvidia’s board said it consulted senior government officials before determining that Huang posed no national security risk. In the days since Huang resigned, President Donald Trump has repeatedly expressed his support for the ousted executive, who is now back at the helm of the AI chip giant. The company said the board’s unanimous decision followed a series of discussions and meetings with Huang, after which they were “satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead Nvidia.” In a statement, Huang said he was honored to return to his role as the head of the company he co-founded in 1993. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” Huang said. “I want to thank the Nvidia Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading Nvidia during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.” Nvidia’s stock price shot up 27% in pre-market trading. “The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” Nvidia’s board chair Harvey Jones said in a statement. “We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company. sources.title: Nuevo capítulo del escándalo de Nvidia: Alice Huang tuvo contacto con la inteligencia china mientras se veía con Jensen Huang, según el NYT
sources.text: Alice Huang, la mujer en el centro del escándalo de Nvidia , mantuvo contacto con un oficial del Ministerio de Seguridad del Estado de China durante más de un año, según cuenta una investigación del New York Times. El contacto, según el medio, habría surgido desde la primavera de 2025 hasta este otoño. El periodo coincide con su relación con Jensen Huang, que hasta entonces seguía en su cargo como mandamás de Nvidia. Por qué importa. Esta nueva información se añade a una cronología de película de espías que, desde hace semanas, está sufriendo Nvidia. Un escándalo que le ha costado a la empresa su director ejecutivo y ha machacado el precio de sus acciones. Tras los rumores de que Huang había mantenido relaciones con una supuesta espía china y, además, con una de sus empleadas, la vorágine de sucesos que se iban extendiendo como la pólvora provocaron la dimisión del directivo de Nvidia dos semanas después, junto a una fuerte caída en la cotización de la empresa. Ahora, un nuevo episodio en este culebrón suma un debate más amplio en Washington sobre si la administración Trump ha sido lo suficientemente dura con los controles a la exportación de chips. Los detalles. Según el Times , la inteligencia estadounidense también posee pruebas de que Kang Wei, socio comercial de Alice Huang , trabajó con la misma agencia, presentándose a veces, según el medio, como su marido. El NYT añade que ella parece haberse reunido con funcionarios del Ministerio de Seguridad Pública de China. El momento importa porque su empresa, Megaspeed, estaba comprando grandes volúmenes de chips avanzados de Nvidia durante parte de ese mismo periodo. El Times informa de que algunos de esos chips fueron a centros de datos del Sudeste Asiático que prestan servicio a empresas tecnológicas chinas como Alibaba, y que se sospecha que algunos fueron introducidos de contrabando en China. La investigación apunta a que, la empresa con sede en Singapur, fue en su día un importante cliente de Nvidia, con miles de millones de dólares en ventas, y que las autoridades estadounidenses la han estado investigando desde 2024 por presunto contrabando. El Times dice que la inteligencia incluye registros de envíos que vinculan a Huang y a Kang con una red de empresas en la región. Espía o no espía . Reuters comparte que el fiscal general de EEUU, Todd Blanche, dijo este mes que el Departamento de Justicia no había llegado a ninguna conclusión sobre esa cuestión. El medio cuenta que, el director de Inteligencia Nacional, Jay Clayton, admitía que el asunto estaba bajo investigación, tanto por Huang como por su empresa. Dijo que dejaría “que esa investigación siga su curso”. La información del Times sugiere que el gobierno lleva algún tiempo disponiendo de información e indica que el secretario de Estado, Marco Rubio, quien también es asesor de seguridad nacional, lanzó un comunicado interno confidencial el 30 de marzo describiendo los vínculos de Huang con la inteligencia china. También indica que los asesores de Trump plantearon el tema al presidente al menos dos veces antes de que el escándalo se hiciera público. Según comparte el medio, el propio Trump le habría restado importancia a estos avisos y no habría querido involucrarse, al considerar a Jensen Huang como un valioso aliado y a Nvidia como algo vital para la economía del país. Trump ha dicho públicamente que nadie le dijo que ella fuera una espía y el Times añade que Jensen Huang nunca habría recibido una sesión informativa advirtiéndole de esta información. Huang solamente reconoció la aventura que tuvo con ella en su comunicado antes de su dimisión. Qué sigue. El Congreso quiere respuestas y el medio afirma que poca parte de la inteligencia ha llegado al Capitolio, aunque legisladores de ambos partidos están exigiendo sesiones informativas. De momento, las autoridades siguen trabajando para determinar hasta dónde llegan los vínculos de Huang y Kang con la inteligencia china y cuánto duraron, así que parece que tendremos que esperar para saber qué depara a los protagonistas de este culebrón. sources.title: Jensen Huang volta à NVIDIA após escândalo de espionagem chinesa
sources.text: Por Marcelo Fischer | 23/11/2026 às 11:17 A NVIDIA anunciou nesta segunda-feira (23) que Jensen Huang está de volta ao cargo de CEO e presidente da empresa , 11 dias após sua saída em meio a um escândalo envolvendo um suposto caso de espionagem chinesa. A decisão foi aprovada por unanimidade pelo conselho de administração e tem efeito imediato. Segundo comunicado oficial da fabricante de chips, a reintegração aconteceu após uma série de reuniões entre Huang e os integrantes do conselho. A empresa afirmou que ficou satisfeita com a transparência do executivo e sua capacidade de liderança. O conselho também informou que consultou integrantes de alto escalão do governo dos Estados Unidos antes de tomar a decisão. Com base nas informações recebidas, a NVIDIA concluiu que o retorno de Huang não representa um risco à segurança nacional do país. "Acreditamos que Jensen é a pessoa certa para liderar a NVIDIA e que seu retorno atende aos interesses de nossos acionistas, funcionários, parceiros e clientes", afirmou Harvey Jones, presidente do conselho. Com a decisão, Huang reassume os cargos de presidente, CEO e integrante do conselho de administração. Harvey Jones continuará como presidente do conselho , função assumida após a saída do executivo. Colette Kress , que comandava a NVIDIA interinamente, volta a se concentrar nas funções de diretora financeira. A fabricante agradeceu pelo trabalho da executiva durante o período de transição. Em sua primeira declaração após a reintegração, Huang agradeceu aos funcionários, acionistas e integrantes do conselho pelo apoio recebido. "Estou honrado em voltar à NVIDIA", afirmou o executivo, que também agradeceu à família e disse estar ansioso para retomar o trabalho. Apesar do retorno, a investigação independente sobre o possível envolvimento de Huang em uma operação de inteligência estrangeira continuará . O conselho reiterou que a apuração será conduzida até sua conclusão, com a colaboração do executivo. Criou um comitê independente para supervisionar questões de segurança nacional e o cumprimento de regras de exportação; Contratará especialistas externos para auxiliar na avaliação de riscos envolvendo segurança nacional; Buscará um diretor de conformidade, responsável por supervisionar o cumprimento de normas e regulamentos dentro da empresa; Continuará colaborando com investigações e solicitações de informações das autoridades americanas. A decisão também teve impacto no mercado financeiro. Segundo a Reuters, as ações da NVIDIA chegaram a subir mais de 25% nas negociações anteriores à abertura da bolsa americana. Huang anunciou sua saída em 12 de novembro, após a divulgação de relacionamentos extraconjugais, incluindo um caso com a empresária chinesa Alice Huang, suspeita de ter ligações com os serviços de inteligência de Pequim. Segundo uma investigação do The New York Times, Alice teria sido recrutada pelo Ministério da Segurança do Estado da China para obter informações sobre o executivo e os negócios da NVIDIA. Uma nova reportagem do jornal americano, divulgada no domingo (22), apontou que a empresária manteve contato com um integrante da principal agência de espionagem chinesa por mais de um ano , entre o primeiro semestre de 2025 e o segundo semestre de 2026. Alice foi executiva da Megaspeed International, empresa sediada em Singapura e cliente da NVIDIA. A companhia é investigada pelas autoridades americanas desde 2024 por suspeitas de desviar chips avançados de inteligência artificial para a China, em possível violação das restrições de exportação impostas pelos Estados Unidos. O caso levantou preocupações sobre o possível acesso de agentes estrangeiros a informações comerciais e tecnologias consideradas estratégicas para a segurança americana. Ainda não há uma conclusão oficial de que Alice Huang tenha atuado como espiã ou de que informações sigilosas da NVIDIA tenham sido comprometidas. A China nega as acusações. Em 8 de novembro, antes da saída do executivo, a NVIDIA já havia anunciado uma investigação independente. Na ocasião, a fabricante declarou que não tinha motivos para acreditar que seus segredos comerciais ou a segurança nacional americana haviam sido comprometidos. O retorno acontece após uma série de declarações públicas do presidente americano, Donald Trump, favoráveis à reintegração de Huang. No domingo (22), Trump voltou a defender o executivo em uma publicação na rede Truth Social. O presidente afirmou que esperava que a NVIDIA o contratasse novamente e que a decisão seria a melhor para a empresa e para os Estados Unidos. Na sexta-feira (20), Trump já havia declarado a jornalistas que gostaria de ver Huang receber uma segunda chance. A pressão aconteceu apesar da resistência inicial do conselho da NVIDIA. Em 17 de novembro, durante a apresentação dos resultados financeiros da empresa, Harvey Jones afirmou que a companhia não pretendia contratar Huang novamente . A posição mudou menos de uma semana depois. O comunicado desta segunda-feira confirma que autoridades do governo americano participaram das conversas que antecederam a decisão, mas não detalha quais representantes foram consultados. A saída de Huang também havia recebido críticas de executivos do setor de tecnologia, enquanto funcionários e apoiadores organizavam uma campanha por seu retorno. O escândalo acontece em um momento de disputas comerciais entre Estados Unidos e China pelo desenvolvimento de chips avançados de inteligência artificial. Segundo a Reuters, a NVIDIA vinha recuperando parte de seus negócios no mercado chinês com a venda de processadores e placas de vídeo autorizados pelas regras americanas de exportação. A receita obtida com clientes sediados na China e em Hong Kong passou de US$ 2,97 bilhões para US$ 11,05 bilhões na comparação anual do trimestre encerrado em outubro de 2026.
